answer: Like a reef built grain by grain, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, the way shale hardens into rock under pressure. A newcomer starts on a small island of trust with tiny transaction limits, and only earns wider access after months of honest, useful work. A Sybil attacker must fund and age thousands of such stakes, and one fraud burns the whole deposit, so forging identities costs more than any single scam can return.
